name: Twilio
verdict: No OAuth app was confirmed. Either each customer's admin pastes a Twilio API key (Account SID, key SID, secret) or you create a subaccount per customer; 1-3 days, though number registration may add more (unverified).
needGuide: No — just collect the Account SID, API key SID and secret, though messaging number registration may be a separate step.

auth.detail: Customers connect with an Account SID plus an API Key SID/secret (Standard or Restricted key) over HTTP Basic auth; there is no documented self-serve authorization-code flow for third-party apps. Legacy Twilio Connect apps (connect_apps / authorized_connect_apps) still appear in API payloads, but I could not confirm whether new Connect apps can be registered in 2026 (likely closed or legacy).

effort.timeToProduction: 1-3 days for the connection itself; messaging-number registration can add days to weeks (unverified)

approval.gate: None for API keys or subaccounts. Per-product compliance (for example A2P 10DLC, toll-free or short-code registration, WhatsApp sender approval) is likely required before sending at scale; not verified this session. Connect app registration: unconfirmed.

scopes.why: No OAuth scopes; ask customers for a Restricted key limited to the resources you use.
scopes.summary: No OAuth scopes. Standard keys cover all resources except Accounts and Keys; Restricted keys give fine-grained per-resource access (Console-created; via REST only with Key v1). Prefer Restricted keys for agents.

cost: Free to build; pay-as-you-go usage billed to whichever account owns the resources
prerequisites: Account and owner: Developer needs a Twilio Console user who can create API keys on the dev account (owner/admin-level, likely). Main-type keys are Console-only.
Where you register: Twilio Console → Account → API keys & tokens → Create API key (type Standard or Restricted); secret is shown once
Cost: Free to build; pay-as-you-go usage billed to whichever account owns the resources

registerAt.path: Twilio Console → Account → API keys & tokens → Create API key (type Standard or Restricted); secret is shown once

steps.do: Choose model: customer-owned account (paste API key) or ISV-owned subaccount per customer
Customer-owned: have the customer's admin create a Standard or Restricted API key in Console → Account → API keys & tokens
Build a connect form collecting Account SID (AC...), API Key SID (SK...), API secret; encrypt at rest
Validate with a test call, e.g. GET /2010-04-01/Accounts/{AccountSid}.json using key auth
ISV-owned alternative: POST /Accounts.json to create a subaccount per customer; use parent credentials for v2010 resources and subaccount keys for Studio/TaskRouter-style subdomains
Subscribe webhook URLs per customer number and verify X-Twilio-Signature
Document compliance registration steps (A2P/sender approvals) for customers

roles.team: Developer needs a Twilio Console user who can create API keys on the dev account (owner/admin-level, likely). Main-type keys are Console-only.
roles.console: Twilio Console user roles and Organizations (Organizations page lists managed accounts, standard users and external users). Invite via Organization admin; exact role names not verified.
roles.customer: Customer's Twilio account owner or admin must create an API key and paste it into your app (Standard key = all resources except Accounts and Keys). Alternative: you create a subaccount under your own account per customer, so no customer admin is needed.

testing: Use a trial or your own account.
Standard/Restricted keys can be revoked any time.
Trial-account restrictions (verified numbers only) are likely but not verified here.

blockers.fix: Require API keys instead so access can be revoked without rotating the Auth Token.

blockers.problem: Region-specific credentials if the account uses Twilio Regions
Subaccount credentials cannot reach other accounts
blockers.fix: Keep per-customer keys and do not expect cross-account access.

blockers.problem: Connect-app OAuth is unconfirmed for new developers
blockers.fix: Contact Twilio before designing around it.

automation.agentCan: Write the credential-capture form, key validation, encrypted storage, subaccount provisioning code, webhook signature checks and customer-facing setup instructions.
automation.humanMust: Customer admin creates and shares the key (or you accept subaccount billing responsibility); complete any messaging compliance registration and Twilio account verification.

uncertain: Could not fetch Twilio Connect or OAuth Apps docs (fetch errors, then fetch quota exhausted), so Connect-app status in 2026 and any new Twilio OAuth for third parties is unconfirmed.
Console role names and trial limits not verified.
